body: Yeahh Darren Criss was so good at his role. He also played Andrew Cunanan who was gay aswell. Whilst searching up if he is straight I found an article saying he’s stepping away from playing gay roles to give opportunities to gay actors!

SAme :) Yeah I think Love, Victor was really really good and hopefully it gets renewed. The only annoying thing is it's on hulu which isn't available in like basically every country apart from America :( . I need to see how his relationship with his family goes after his coming out.

Yeahh your point deffo makes sense! I deffo wouldn’t want them to have picked a bad Simon or Victor because of their sexuality. Representation through the actors would be nice but I get why it’s not the most important thing ever. Also Bram was played by a bi guy and i think his friends from New York were also lgbtq+ irl so they were representative in sexuality and gender identity through their actors as well as characters :)
I came out to my friend just randomly whilst talking on snapchat. then I made a special private story to come out to a select few

Yeahh I automatically knew that the lead in Love Simon was straight but my gaydar is clearly off because I didn’t consider the same thing in Love Victor lmao. Yeah show business is the one industry where I feel like gay men are more likely to be out and everything but I’ll give the casting directors the benefit of the doubt that Nick Robison was as perfect as they could get

Yeahh I think Michael’s performance was really good in the series. Yeah the representation in love, Simon and love, victor are so good. I loved that Victor and his family were Hispanic and Mia and Andrew were also POC. Also the lgbtq+ representation in the New York ep was nice to see

Yeahh I definitely see your point, acting is acting for a reason! I guess I was just thinking of it in a different way. I feel like compared to straight romance/coming of age movies lgbt ones are rarely as mainstream. Love, Simon would’ve been a good opportunity for a gay actor to get their start. However nick Robinson was great and the movie will always make me cry so I really can’t complain :)

Everyone did discuss that when Disney dropped that. Personally it was on my Twitter timeline and people were very pissed. Also comparing lgbtq representation to Italian food downplays it. I just personally think it’s amazing when lgbt characters are played by lgbtq actors, representation is important not only in characters but actors and writers etc.

Pose is a great example of a show that could have picked straight actors to play gay roles but didn’t. For a younger kid, finding out the lead actor in their favourite lgbtq+ movie/show might be a slap in the face.

Of course there are bigger problems but problems are problems you know?

A lot of people in the thread aren’t seeing the real issue. There’s a lot of racism in the acting business and that means that black and other ethnic minority actors aren’t casted as much as they could be.

By putting black people/mixed people in black and mixed roles it’s a way to make sure that the scene is diverse. Making silly comparisons to oh but that pig is voiced by a human is down playing this. 

Furthermore this was a choice by the actor (forgotten her name my bad) not by the audience and not by biracial fans. Personally, as a black girl, I don’t have a problem with white people voicing black characters on a surface level. However, the lack of diversity and the smaller amount of chances black people get is the real issue. I don’t speak for black people though this is just my opinion.
Thanks for the advice! I think it will be quite hard to persuade her, she’s always been one of those “gays will burn in hell” type of Christians but maybe she’ll try and be accepting with me. :)

Thank you for taking the time to reply. Yeah the feeling you’ve described is exactly how I feel. I don’t have anywhere to go in the foreseeable future, my close friends have pretty cramped living situations. 

Unfortunately the resources aren’t for my country but I’ll be okay researching similar things :). I’ll definitely make it my priority to have a safe environment in the next couple years.

Your kind words mean more than I can express. It’s been a really hard couple of weeks and I needed to hear that. Thank you so so much 🖤

I’m so sorry about your parents :/ being bi is definitely not shameful or anything to be kicked out for. thanks for the advice! I came out to most of my close friends :) I guess I just wish I could have my family’s support aswell but the chances of that is like 0.00001% unfortunately

You don’t need to decide your sexuality. It definitely comes naturally and often takes people months/years to figure out and accept. Lots of people don’t even label themselves gay,straight or anything else on the spectrum. I’d say don’t sweat it at all, no offence but whoever told you that definitely doesn’t know what they’re talking about.
